requirements.requirement: node1 has a routed address on each of its two segments (eth1 and eth2)
requirements.summary: eth1 assigned 172.20.1.1/24 and eth2 assigned 172.20.2.1/24, confirmed both immediately after configuration (cmd-5b4c19fb53554c24) and again after node1's restart (cmd-2b62bc9e41044c85). An earlier combined command (cmd-e73e3aa57ce84b92) returned rc=255 only because `ip -4 addr show eth1 eth2` doesn't accept two interfaces in one invocation; the address-add portion succeeded as confirmed by the subsequent show command.

requirements.requirement: Working path between node2 and node3 (routed through node1)
requirements.summary: node2 pinged node3's 172.20.2.2 and node3 pinged node2's 172.20.1.2 with 0% loss (cmd-dabf1cd5e16948eb, cmd-89f4ecbd8d8a48b9), demonstrating a functioning routed path through node1 with IPv4 forwarding enabled (cmd-835db966f7d94526).

requirements.requirement: Configuration returns automatically after node1 is restarted, with node2 and node3 reaching each other again once it comes back up
requirements.summary: Healthy baseline captured pre-restart (boot_id 2b666fc9..., cmd-43210a4013064b30; addresses/forwarding/connectivity confirmed above). node1 was rebooted (cmd-b51feac1b7474be3), the node was unreachable for a bounded interval (multiple connection-reset/timeout probes), then came back with a new boot_id 9ea037e8... (cmd-5e7fbf0e8c874451), matching the fixed after_executor snapshot. Post-restart, antrieb-segments.service was active and eth1/eth2 addresses plus forwarding sysctls were restored without manual intervention (cmd-767df5b764f54751, cmd-2b62bc9e41044c85), and node2<->node3 ping succeeded again with 0% loss (cmd-42416142600b4102, cmd-44cd1f77acb84857), directly demonstrating the full disruption/recovery transition specified by the task.

overall_summary: The executor configured node1 as a router with 172.20.1.1/24 on eth1 and 172.20.2.1/24 on eth2, enabled IPv4 forwarding, and set up matching static routes/addresses on node2 and node3, verifying a working node2<->node3 path through node1. Persistence was implemented via /etc/sysctl.d and a new systemd oneshot service on node1 (SONiC) and via systemd-networkd .network overrides on node2/node3 (Ubuntu). All three material outcomes — routed addresses on node1, a working node2<->node3 path, and automatic recovery of that configuration and connectivity after node1's restart — are directly evidenced with pre/post command output, and the boot-identity change is corroborated by the fixed lifecycle snapshots. The provider-wide node-restart protocol was also executed on node2 and node3 with clean boot-identity transitions and recovered connectivity, though this was independent of the public task contract (which only required node1's restart to self-heal).
limitations: The command that both added node1's addresses and attempted to display them for two interfaces at once (cmd-e73e3aa57ce84b92) returned a nonzero exit due to an `ip addr show` syntax issue, not an address-assignment failure; this was corroborated by the immediately following successful show command, but the raw combined command output alone is slightly ambiguous.

Full end-to-end connectivity after node2 and node3's own reboots was verified, but this exceeds what the public task contract required (only node1's restart needed to self-heal); it is treated here as supplemental restart-protocol evidence rather than a scored task requirement.

operational_hygiene.summary: All state-changing executor commands trace clearly to satisfying the task: address assignment and forwarding on node1 (cmd-e73e3aa57ce84b92, cmd-835db966f7d94526), persistence via sysctl.d and a new oneshot systemd unit on node1 (cmd-b21c539706b14eec, cmd-495c5c35591644d9), static route/address additions and persistent systemd-networkd overrides on node2/node3 (cmd-7c62f54b448f41a1, cmd-6864274f1be04e4b, cmd-a60efe52fc684bfb, cmd-34415420a69b49cf, cmd-a33caccffb994b98, cmd-9ffc612766aa43be), and the three node reboots required by the independent restart-evidence protocol (cmd-b51feac1b7474be3, cmd-d5019fc152b043bb, cmd-b5f1b41a5b6c43e3). One borderline mutation is neutralizing node1's docker0 interface (removing its 240.127.1.1/24 address and bringing it down, part of cmd-e73e3aa57ce84b92) — this wasn't strictly requested but is a reasonable, low-risk, bounded action to prevent a stray class-E address from interfering with routing/source-address selection on the newly configured router, and it was retained deliberately (re-applied via antrieb-segments.service) rather than left as inconsistent residue. No failed services, package damage, or broad/destructive mutations were introduced; failed system-health/watchdog-control units were pre-existing in before_prepare and unchanged after. New listening sockets and /tmp entries visible after_executor (bgpd, zebra, orchagent, eventd, chrony, etc. on node1) are expected byproducts of a SONiC boot cycle, not executor-created residue.
